name: environment
text:
Commands run in sh (/bin/sh -c) on macOS.
This is plain POSIX sh: [[ ]], arrays, source, {a,b}, <(…) and echo -e may not work; use [ ], ., printf, or run bash -c '…'.
macOS has BSD tools, not GNU: sed -i '' (not sed -i), stat -f (not -c), date -v-1d (not -d), no grep -P (use -E or perl), no nproc (sysctl -n hw.ncpu).

name: sandbox
text:
Sandbox: read-only. Commands can read any file and write only $TMPDIR.
$TMPDIR (/tmp/s/x) is this session's private scratch directory, writable in every mode: put temporary files there, and point a tool cache that cannot be written elsewhere at it, such as GOCACHE=$TMPDIR/go-build.
ps and pgrep fail in the sandbox (lsof works); request escalation to list processes.
Local sockets count as network: docker and other clients of a daemon's socket fail in the sandbox, so request escalation for them from the first try.

text:
Commands run in fish (/usr/bin/fish -c) on macOS.
fish is not a POSIX shell. These fail in fish:
- Heredocs (<<EOF, <<<): pipe printf '%s\n' … into the command, or write the file with your file tool.
- for …; do …; done, while …; do …; done, if …; then …; fi, case: fish uses for x in …; …; end, while …; …; end, if …; …; end, switch.
- x=1 on its own: use set x 1 (set -x to export). VAR=1 cmd works.
- $?, ${x}, $((1+2)), backticks, <(cmd): use $status, {$x}, math 1+2, (cmd), (cmd | psub).
- An unmatched glob is an error: quote patterns (find -name '*.go').
For a POSIX script, run it as one sh -c '…' (inside fish single quotes, \' and \\ are escapes).
macOS has BSD tools, not GNU: sed -i '' (not sed -i), stat -f (not -c), date -v-1d (not -d), no grep -P (use -E or perl), no nproc (sysctl -n hw.ncpu).

text:
Commands run in nushell (/usr/bin/nu -c) on macOS.
nushell is not a POSIX shell; its commands return structured data. These fail in nushell:
- && and ||: separate commands with ;.
- x=1, export X=1, $X: use $env.X = '1' and $env.X.
- $(cmd), backticks: use (cmd).
- 2>&1, 2>/dev/null: use o+e>| and e> /dev/null.
- Heredocs, for …; do …; done, if …; then …; fi.
ls, rm, cp and others are nushell builtins with other flags: prefix ^ (^ls) for the external command. For a POSIX script, run it as one sh -c '…'.

name: harness
text:
Bash output: max_output_length caps each output field at that many characters (default 40000); cut output keeps its head and tail around a marker, with the path of the file that holds all of it.
- Leave it unset when you need the whole output: a file you will edit, a failing test's full report.
- Set it only for noisy commands (builds, logs, broad searches), sized to what you will actually read.
- When output was cut, narrow the command (a pattern, a line range, one test) or read the saved file in parts; do not run it again with a bigger limit.
